DEPARTMENT OF RADIOLOGY & IMAGINE

2-D; COLOUR AND SPECTRAL DOPPLER STUDY OF LOWER

LIMB [VEIN ]

[Bilateral / Right / Left]

VEINS EXAMINED

* Common femoral vein.

* Superficial femoral vein.

* Deep femoral vein.

* Popliteal vein.

* Deep veins of leg.

 

REPORT :

All major deep veins of thigh and calf region shows normal luminal calibre with normal flow. Flow in uniphasic with normal flow velocity. No intraluminal thrombus seen. No significant vessel wall irregularity / thickening seen. Compressibility and augmentation responses

are well preserved.

 

Both sapheno – femoral and sapheno – popliteal junctions are well visualised. Normal flow pattern is obscured with normal augmentation response. At sapheno – femoral junction, Valsalva response is elicited with no associated venous reflux. Valve in sapheno – femoral junction shows normal movement.

 

Deep veins accompanying major calf arteries are visualised with normal compressibility and augmentation response. No internal thrombus / wall irregularity seen.

 

Few perforater veins could be demonstrated at calf region.

Perforater veins are showing superficial to deep flow with no associated reflux.

Few venous sinuses are noted within gastrocneumius—soleus muscle complex.

 

No superficial varicosities seen.

No significant subcutaneous oedema seen.

Skin and subcutaneous tissue not thickened.

No enlarged inguinal nodes seen.

 

IMPRESSION :

LOWER LIMB VENOUS DOPPLER STUDY SHOWS NO OBVIOUS ABNORMALITY.

 

                                                                                   DR.  S.BHATTACHARYA

Checked by                                                                 MD [RADIOLOGY]

                                                 CONSULTANT RADIOLOGIST & SONOLOGIST

ULTRASONOGRAPHY OF LOWER LIMB ARTERIAL DOPPLER

RIGHT LOWER LIMB/LEFT LOWER LIMB

 

 

 

Common femoral artery, superficial femoral artery, deep femoral artery, popliteal artery, anterior tibial artery, posterior tibial artery, common peroneal artery, dorsalis pedis artery are normal in calibre, size, shape, intimal thickness, luminal echo and distal branching pattern. Normal Triphasic peak systolic velocity with low diastolic velocity of peripheral resistance is noted. No dumpening, loss of Triphasic pattern, regurgitation, occusion are seen. No obvious arterio venous malformation or arteriovenous fistula,  aneurysmal dilatation are noted. No definite subcutaneous edema are seen.

ULTRASONOGRAPHY OF LOWER LIMB VENOUS DOPPLER

RIGHT LOWER LIMB/LEFT LOWER LIMB

 

 

Common femoral vein, deep femoral vein, superficial femoral vein, popliteal vein, posterior tibial vein, anterior tibial vein, common peroneal vein are normal in size, shape, calibre, luminal flow, echopattern and distal branching pattern. Normal in spectral flow pattern with normal compressibility, respiratory phasicity, valsalva, distal and proximal augmentation with no reversal, regurgitation, spectral drop, artero venous malformation are noted. Great saphenous vein and small saphenous vein are normal in shape, position, calibre, luminal flow pattern including distal branches with normal compressibility, respiratory phasicity, valsalva, distal and proximal augmentation with no reversal, regurgitation, spectal drop with normal and competent sapheno femoral junction and sapheno popliteal junction. No obvious flow reversal is noted or incompetence seen. Superficial veins are not dilated and competent. No obvious subcutaneous edema is noted.
